intent: Bring pacman_wrapper.sh (929 lines) under the 250-line cap. This file IS /usr/bin/pacman on this machine — /usr/bin/pacman is a symlink to the deployed copy — so the overriding constraint is that no failure mode may leave the box without a working package manager.
scope: New libs, FLAT beside the wrapper: pw_policy.sh (188), pw_challenge.sh (177), pw_cleanup.sh (153), pw_guard.sh (145), pw_ui.sh (90)
install_pacman_wrapper.sh + lib/install_files.sh: deploy the five libs
lib/integrity.sh: checksum them in the policy manifest
Non-goal: redeploying to /usr/local/bin, and any live `pacman -S` transaction
changes: All 31 functions moved into five libs by responsibility. This needed a fix to extract_shell_functions.py first (committed separately): 17 of the 31 use bash's `function name() {` spelling, which the extractor did not recognise and would have silently left behind.
Libs are deployed FLAT beside the wrapper, matching pacman_lock_lib.sh and heavy_job_lock.sh, which already live and are sourced that way in /usr/local/bin. No lib/ subdirectory is created there.
The source block sits at the TOP of the file, before the fast path, because the fast path calls needs_unlock() to decide whether to exec real pacman and that function now lives in pw_guard.sh.

FAIL OPEN, unlike every other split in this campaign. A missing lib prints a warning to stderr and execs real pacman unwrapped. Failing closed here would mean a missing lib leaves no way to install anything — including the missing lib. This mirrors the choice the pre-existing pacman_lock_lib.sh block already makes.

The five libs are registered in install_files.sh as REQUIRED copies and added to the integrity manifest. They are sourced before verify_policy_integrity runs (the fast path forces that ordering), so the manifest entry is what makes tampering detectable — the check still refuses the transaction afterwards.
BOLD and MAKEPKG_CAPPED_BIN are exported: they are read by pw_ui.sh and pw_cleanup.sh, which shellcheck cannot see across the source boundary without -x.

verification.evidence: REAL pacman queries through the split wrapper, byte-identical to the pre-split baseline: -Qi bash matches exactly, and -Q lists the same 2824 packages. This is execution, not textual proof — better than the --help-only baseline the prompt expected for this file.

verification.command: fail-open simulation: flat layout in a scratch dir with pw_guard.sh removed
verification.evidence: THE critical safety property. With needs_unlock's lib missing, the wrapper prints 'pacman wrapper libraries missing; running pacman unwrapped.' to stderr, execs real pacman, returns rc=0 and real -Qi output. A missing lib cannot brick package management.

verification.command: integrity round-trip in a fake root
verification.evidence: Built the manifest exactly as the patched installer does: 8 entries (2 policy lists + lock lib + 5 new libs). Untampered libs verify clean. Appending one line to pw_challenge.sh is DETECTED and the wrapper denies operation. The new libs are genuinely covered, not a hole in the check.
'IDENTICAL: all 14 top-level functions moved verbatim' — no body changed.
Two apparent losses, both explained: BOLD and MAKEPKG_CAPPED_BIN now carry an `export` prefix. Both confirmed present in the entry script; no code line was lost.

verification.command: sha256sum /usr/local/bin/pacman_wrapper vs the backup taken before any edit
verification.evidence: 548fc2b53ee4cea6... on both. The deployed copy is untouched by this commit, which is why live pacman is unaffected. `pacman -Qi bash` through the real /usr/bin/pacman symlink still works, and the symlink is intact.

verification.command: shellcheck (no -x), shfmt idempotence, hyphenated-key canary, check_file_length --all
verification.evidence: shellcheck rc=0 with no new suppression; shfmt a no-op on all eight touched files; canary clean. The over-cap list is down to a single file.

risks: NOT VERIFIED against a live `pacman -S` transaction. The Bash tool deadlocks on db.lck for interactive pacman, and a failed experiment here costs the package manager. The evidence is instead: identical real read-only queries, a proven fail-open path, and a proven integrity round-trip. Running `sudo install_pacman_wrapper.sh` followed by a real install remains the one check only the user can perform.

The deployed copy still lacks the pw_*.sh libs until install_pacman_wrapper.sh is re-run. That ordering is safe in both directions: the deployed monolith is unchanged and self-contained, and if the new entry script were deployed without libs it would fail open to plain pacman rather than break.

The libs are sourced before verify_policy_integrity, so a tampered lib executes before the manifest is checked. Unavoidable given the fast path needs needs_unlock, and the same was already true of the wrapper file itself; the transaction is still refused.
rollback: git revert the commit; pacman_wrapper.sh returns to one 929-line file and the pw_*.sh libs disappear.
No live rollback needed — the deployed copy was never written.

If the split HAD been deployed: `sudo cp /tmp/.../restore/pacman_wrapper.deployed.bak /usr/local/bin/pacman_wrapper` restores the byte-identical monolith, and /usr/bin/pacman.orig (a real 157 KB ELF, verified running Pacman v7.1.0) is the escape hatch if even that fails.
